messages:
Eve (PM): Heads up — BigCorp asked us to 'lock-step' their model migration to exact calendar dates. They're asking we slow onboarding velocity for the next quarter to avoid breaking their contract. Thoughts?
Ben (Eng Lead): slowing velocity affects the onboarding backlog. We have 6 models queued that rely on the faster cadence. Can we do a scoped slowdown instead of full halt?
Aisha (Product Ops): +1 scoped slowdown. We should define what 'lock-step' means: is it a hard freeze, or a coordinated canary and then a single cutover?
Carlos (Solutions Eng): From the field: BigCorp needs a 4-week grace window + a pinned model version during cutover. They also want the canary in their dedicated pool.
Dana (Customer Success): Confirmed — they cited procurement language: "no forced model swaps during quarter X." They will accept a canary but only with explicit runbook and rollback commitments.
Eve (PM): OK lets enumerate options: 1) Full freeze for quarter (blocks everyone), 2) Cohort-based slow lanes (limit new onboardings to low-risk models), 3) Canaries in dedicated pools + contract clause (preferred). Thoughts on acceptance criteria for option 3?
Ben (Eng Lead): For canary option we need technical acceptance: latency P95 < 200ms, token cost delta < 10%, and no more than 0.5% increase in error rate during canary. Also hardware isolation for canary.
Aisha (Product Ops): Add rollout gates: success on 3 internal tenants, then 2 external small customers, then BigCorp. Timeboxed to 2 weeks per stage.
Carlos (Solutions Eng): I'll draft the canary runbook. Needs: dedicated pool name, model pin ID, traffic split commands, and monitoring dashboard links. Example commands:```sh
# assign canary pool
rictl assign --pool bigcorp-canary --model openv2-3b:2026-04
# split traffic
rictl route --from prod --to bigcorp-canary --pct 5
```
Ben (Eng Lead): We also need an automated fallback: if error_rate > 0.5% OR latency P95 exceeds 250ms for 10m, route back to previous pin. Can we get that in the router?
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: Canary pool "bigcorp-canary" created by Carlos at 1759010200 :rocket:
Dana (Customer Success): Contract team wants a 6-week overlap (grace), but legal may accept 4 if we provide SLA credits for any forced change. We should map this to a comms doc.
Eve (PM): Action items: Carlos -> runbook (due EOD tomorrow), Ben -> auto-fallback impl spec + ops alert thresholds (due 48h), Aisha -> comms + contract language draft (due 72h), Dana -> confirm customer willingness for canary + credits (sync with legal).
Aisha (Product Ops): I'll prepare a small template for pin-exception requests to be triaged. Fields: customer, model, target cutover date, grace window length, acceptance metrics.
Ben (Eng Lead): If we do cohort-slow lanes, we should throttle onboarding pipelines instead of canceling. Example: `onboard_rate_limit = 2 models/week` for Q. That preserves throughput while meeting lock-step ask.
Carlos (Solutions Eng): For the canary runbook, propose this sequence: provision -> internal smoke -> 5% external traffic -> 25% -> 100% cutover. Each step must have signoff from Eng + CS.
Eve (PM): Good. One more ask from sales: can we add a temporary pin-exception flag in the console UI so account teams can see locked models? UI change low-priority but helpful.
Ben (Eng Lead): Agree low effort to show a read-only "lock" badge. We'll backlog it under devex.
Dana (Customer Success): I'll tell BigCorp this plan and ask for written signoff on canary + rollback terms. If they sign, we proceed with option 3.
Eve (PM): Sounds like consensus. We'll treat this as a scoped velocity adjustment (not a full freeze). If any of the acceptance metrics fail, we abort and revert. Meeting to ratify plan at 11:00 tomorrow. :calendar:
Carlos (Solutions Eng): I'll drop the draft runbook link in the thread once ready.
Eve (PM): Thanks all — please update the action items in the shared board. :white_check_mark:
